claims.statement: Joint CircuitBreaker theorem under rules.md: the following declaration defines ONE fixed eligible total uniform NP family in the pinned full B2 model at actual input length n. Its full guarantee and its declared projection both hold unconditionally, for all sufficiently large integer lengths with the quantifiers specified by the theorem kinds. Both score source claims assert this ENTIRE declaration, not separate lemmas. Let L(n)=c*n^p*(log2 n)^q*(log2 log2 n)^r with the exact parameters in guarantee.leading. Let R(n) be the sum of the monomials in guarantee.remainder.terms, each coefficient times n^exponent*(log2 n)^log_exponent*(log2 log2 n)^loglog_exponent; an empty sum is zero. There exists N such that C_B2(f_n)>=L(n)-R(n) for every integer n>=N. All remainder coefficients are the exact declared constants. Declaration: {"convention":"uniform-np-full-b2-actual-length-all-lengths-v1","family":"The single total certificate-prefix language specified in proof.md. For actual length N, choose k as the least prime at least the least positive B with B^5>32*N^3; read k input bits as the lower coefficients of a monic degree-k polynomial Q over F_2, reject invalid Q by the exact Frobenius/gcd test, and evaluate the descending-power BK symmetric polynomial on the remaining N-k bits with zero padding, r=ceil((N-k)/k), t=ceil(sqrt(r)). Output 0 for N=0 or the explicit failed guards in proof.md. The output is the constant coefficient in F_2[Z]/Q. All k prefix bits are included in N; Q is input, not advice.","guarantee":{"kind":"eventual_lower_bound","leading":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"4"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"polynomial_log","log_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"},"loglog_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"}},"remainder":{"kind":"explicit","terms":[{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"45"},"exponent":{"denominator":"5","numerator":"4"},"log_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"},"loglog_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"}},{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"52"},"exponent":{"denominator":"5","numerator":"3"},"log_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"},"loglog_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"}},{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"27"},"exponent":{"denominator":"5","numerator":"2"},"log_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"},"loglog_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"}},{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"44"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"},"log_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"},"loglog_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"}}]}},"projection":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"4"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"finite"},"theorem":"This fixed total language is in P, hence in NP with empty witnesses. In the full pinned B2 model, for every integer N>=2^20, C_B2(F_N)>=4N-R(N), where R(N)=4k+9(floor(kr/t)+kt+r(r+1)+2)<=45*N^(4/5)+52*N^(3/5)+27*N^(2/5)+44, with k,r,t exactly as defined by the evaluator in proof.md. Hence also R(N)<=150*N^(4/5) at every such N, and for every real epsilon>0 the threshold N_epsilon=max(2^20,ceil((150/epsilon)^5)) gives C_B2(F_N)>=(4-epsilon)*N for every integer N>=N_epsilon. Thus liminf over all integer N of C_B2(F_N)/N is at least 4, and the loss below 4N is explicitly bounded at every integer N>=2^20, not merely asymptotically.","version":"circuitbreaker-expression-v2"}
